cohort: The study included 1410 cases diagnosed with Eosinophilic esophagitis (EoE) from October 2008 to September 2015, matched 1:2 by age and sex to 2820 controls from the Military Health System Database.
finding: Early infant exposures such as acid-blocking medications (PPIs, H2RAs), antibiotics, prematurity, milk protein allergy, eczema, feeding difficulty, gastroesophageal reflux disease, and erythema toxicum were associated with an increased risk of later Eosinophilic esophagitis (EoE) diagnosis.
followup_time: Up to 7.2 years (median age at diagnosis of 4.2 years)
